paper_metadata.title: Sub-500-ps 64-b ALUs in 0.18-m SOI/Bulk CMOS: Design and Scaling Trends
paper_metadata.abstract: In this paper, we present: 1) design of a single-rail energy-efficient 64-b Han–Carlson ALU, operating at 482 ps in 1.5 V, 0.18m bulk CMOS; 2) direct port of this ALU to 0.18m partially depleted SOI process; 3) SOI-optimal redesign of the ALU using a novel deep-stack quaternary-tree architecture; 4) margining for max-delay pushout due to reverse body bias in SOI designs; and 5) performance scaling trends of the ALU designs in 0.13m generation. We show that a direct port of the Han–Carlson ALU to 0.18m SOI offers 14% performance improvement after margining. A redesign of the ALU, using an SOI-favored deep-stack architecture improves the margined speedup to 19%. A 10% margin was required for the SOI designs, Fig. 1. 64-b ALU architecture. to account for reverse body-bias-induced max-delay pushout. Preconditioning the intermediate stack nodes in the dynamic ALU 1) direct port of the baseline bulk design to a comparable designs reduced this margin to 2%. Scaling the ALUs to 0.13m generation reduces the overall SOI speedup for both architectures SOI technology; to 9% and 16%, respectively, confirming the trend that speedup 2) SOI-optimal redesign of the adder core. offered by SOI technology decreases with scaling. sections.text_preview: SOI technology offers features that expand the design space with respect to a bulk design, motivating an SOI-optimal redesign of the ALU.
